home.eyebrow: YOUR FILES. YOUR TOOLS. YOUR RULES.
home.title: Make room for your best work.
home.intro: Meet OFF42. Six focused apps for documents, spreadsheets, presentations, PDFs, images and scans. One open-source office, right on your Mac.
home.suiteTitle: A whole office. A lighter feeling.
home.suiteIntro: From the first rough draft to the final signed PDF, keep your everyday work in one familiar family of tools.
home.featureIntro: Edit a PDF. Tame a large attachment. Turn a paper page into searchable text. Find the tool for the job.
home.privacyTitle: Your desk. Not someone else's server.
home.privacyText: Core editing happens on your Mac. Work on local files without uploading them to an online editor. Network features, including trusted signature timestamps, need a connection.
home.languageText: The website and app interface speak your language. Choose yours and keep the same tools close at hand.
home.openTitle: An open office, in every sense.
home.openText: OFF42 is released under the MIT license. Read the code, build it yourself, report a bug or help make the next version better.
home.endTitle: Good work starts with the right tools.
home.formatsTitle: Works with the files you already have.
home.formatsText: Open what colleagues send you and save in the format they expect. Complex layouts can look different, so check important files after import.

faq.a: Yes. OFF42 is free and open source under the MIT license. There are no subscriptions, accounts or in-app purchases.

Core editing works on your Mac without an internet connection, and your files are not uploaded anywhere. Network features, such as trusted signature timestamps and opening web links, need a connection.

faq.q: Can OFF42 open Microsoft Office files?
faq.a: Yes. DOC42 opens DOCX and DOC, XLS42 opens XLSX and XLS, and PPT42 opens PPTX. OpenDocument files (ODT, ODS, ODP) are supported too. Not every Office feature is supported, so check complex files after import.
OFF42 targets macOS 14 or later. A public installer has not been released yet; you can build the apps from source with the Xcode Command Line Tools.
A preliminary Windows version is being developed in the same open repository. A Windows installer has not been published yet.

edit-pdf.title: Edit PDFs on your Mac
edit-pdf.seoTitle: Free PDF Editor for Mac — Edit, Annotate, Fill Forms | OFF42
edit-pdf.seoDescription: Edit PDF text, highlight, annotate, fill forms and reorder pages on your Mac with PDF42. Free, open source and offline — no uploads to an online editor.
edit-pdf.intro: Make the PDF your working document. Edit page text, add notes, highlight the important parts, fill forms and put pages in the right order with PDF42.
points: Edit page text and annotate with highlights, text boxes, shapes and freehand marks.
Insert, extract, rotate, delete and reorder pages.
Fill supported PDF forms and save your changes.
steps: Open a PDF from your Mac.
Choose markup, forms or page tools for your task.
Save a copy and review the finished document.
edit-pdf.note: Page-text edits flatten on save. Complex PDF layouts and forms can vary; review a saved copy before sharing.
edit-pdf.question: Can I edit a PDF without uploading it?
edit-pdf.answer: Yes. PDF42 works with local files on your Mac. Core markup and page operations do not need an online editor.

compress-pdf.title: Compress PDFs, keep things moving
compress-pdf.seoTitle: Compress PDF on Mac — Reduce File Size Offline | OFF42
compress-pdf.seoDescription: Shrink image-heavy PDFs on your Mac with PDF42. Choose 100, 150 or 220 dpi, preview the size and keep text sharp. Free, offline, no file uploads.
compress-pdf.intro: Make image-heavy PDFs easier to share. PDF42 offers compression controls so you can choose a practical balance between file size and image detail.
points: Choose 100, 150 or 220 dpi image presets.
Preview file sizes while keeping text and vector content sharp.
Save a separate file and compare the result with the original.
steps: Open your PDF and choose compression.
Choose an image preset and compare the size estimates.
Save the result, then check its size and legibility.
compress-pdf.note: Results depend on the source file and may show no size reduction. Compression reduces image quality and removes existing digital signatures.
compress-pdf.question: How much smaller will my PDF be?
compress-pdf.answer: There is no fixed reduction. Scanned and image-heavy PDFs often offer more room for compression than files that are already optimised.

sign-pdf.title: Make your mark on a PDF
sign-pdf.seoTitle: Sign PDF on Mac — Signatures, Stamps, Digital Signing | OFF42
sign-pdf.seoDescription: Add a handwritten-style signature or a stamp to a PDF, or sign it with a certificate. PDF42 keeps your marks in a reusable library. Free and open source.
sign-pdf.intro: Keep signatures and stamps close to your work. Add a visual signature, reuse a stamp or work with certificate-based digital signatures in PDF42.
points: Keep reusable signatures and stamps in the shared library.
Place and adjust a visual mark on the page.
Use certificate-based signing when your workflow requires it.
steps: Open the document and choose the signature tool.
Select a visual mark or a digital-signature workflow.
Save and check the result in your recipient's PDF software.
sign-pdf.note: A visual signature is not a certificate-backed digital signature. Certificate trust and timestamp interoperability depend on the certificate, service and receiving software.
sign-pdf.question: Are visual and digital signatures the same?
sign-pdf.answer: No. A visual signature is a mark on the page. A digital signature uses a certificate to help detect document changes and identify the signer.

scan-ocr.title: Turn paper into searchable work
scan-ocr.seoTitle: Scanner App with OCR for Mac — Searchable PDF | OFF42
scan-ocr.seoDescription: Scan from a scanner or iPhone camera, straighten and clean pages, recognise text on your Mac and export a searchable PDF with SCN42. Free and offline.
scan-ocr.intro: Bring paper into your digital office with SCN42. Acquire pages, straighten and clean them up, then recognise text on your Mac.
points: Acquire from supported scanners or import images and PDFs.
Crop, deskew and adjust pages before recognition.
Export searchable PDFs or recognised text.
steps: Scan or import your pages.
Check page order and clean up the images.
Run OCR and export the format you need.
scan-ocr.note: Scanner and Continuity support depends on your hardware. OCR languages and accuracy depend on Apple Vision and the source image; the 20 interface languages are a separate feature.
scan-ocr.question: Can I search the text in a scan?
scan-ocr.answer: Export a searchable PDF after OCR to add a text layer. Always review recognition results, particularly names, numbers and low-quality scans.

documents.title: Space for your next good idea
documents.seoTitle: Free Word Processor for Mac — DOCX, ODT, RTF | OFF42
documents.seoDescription: Write letters and reports in DOC42: open and save DOCX, ODT, RTF and Markdown, lay out pages with tables and images, export PDF. Free and open source.
documents.intro: Write letters, reports and the next draft with DOC42. Combine rich text and page layout with familiar document formats.
points: Open and save DOCX, ODT, RTF, Markdown and other text formats.
Work with formatting, tables, images and page layout.
Export to PDF when the document is ready to share.
steps: Create a document or open an existing file.
Shape the text, images and page layout.
Save an editable copy or export a PDF.
documents.note: Complex Office documents can render differently. Check imported layout and the exported file before relying on exact fidelity.
documents.question: Can I work with Word documents?
documents.answer: DOC42 supports DOCX and opens legacy DOC files. File-format support does not imply identical handling of every Microsoft Word feature.

spreadsheets.title: Make sense of the numbers
spreadsheets.seoTitle: Free Spreadsheet App for Mac — XLSX, ODS, CSV | OFF42
spreadsheets.seoDescription: Open XLSX and XLS files, use formulas, formatting and charts, save XLSX, ODS or CSV and export PDF with XLS42. A free, open-source spreadsheet app for Mac.
spreadsheets.intro: From a simple list to a calculated report, XLS42 brings cells, formulas and charts into your everyday office.
points: Open XLSX, legacy XLS, ODS and delimited text files.
Use formulas, formatting and charts to explain your data.
Save XLSX, ODS or CSV, or export a PDF.
steps: Open a workbook or start with a blank sheet.
Enter data, apply formulas and add a chart.
Review calculations and save in the right format.
spreadsheets.note: Formula and formatting support varies by file. CSV stores a single table of values, not a complete workbook with formatting and multiple sheets.
spreadsheets.question: Can I open Excel spreadsheets?
spreadsheets.answer: Yes, XLS42 opens XLSX and legacy XLS files. Check complex formulas and imported formatting; not every Excel feature is supported.

presentations.title: Give your ideas the floor
presentations.seoTitle: Free Presentation App for Mac — PPTX, ODP | OFF42
presentations.seoDescription: Build slides with text, images, shapes and tables, present with speaker notes and export PDF or images with PPT42. Free, open source, made for Mac.
presentations.intro: Build a clear visual story with PPT42. Arrange text, images, shapes and tables, then move from editing to a slide show.
points: Work with PPTX and OpenDocument presentation files.
Arrange slide objects, tables and speaker notes.
Export slides to PDF and images for easy sharing.
steps: Create a deck or open a supported presentation.
Refine each slide and prepare your notes.
Run a slide show or export your slides.
presentations.note: Legacy PPT files need conversion first. Complex imported layouts can differ; review the full deck before presenting.
presentations.question: Can I share slides as a PDF?
presentations.answer: Yes. PPT42 supports PDF export for slides and notes pages, as well as PNG and JPEG slide images.

image-editor.title: The finishing touch, without the fuss
image-editor.seoTitle: Free Image Editor for Mac — Crop, Resize, Annotate | OFF42
image-editor.seoDescription: Open JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WebP and TIFF, then crop, resize, rotate, adjust and annotate with IMG42. A free, open-source image editor that works offline.
image-editor.intro: Open a photo, crop a distraction, adjust the image or add a clear annotation. IMG42 keeps everyday image tasks close at hand.
points: View common image formats, including JPEG, PNG, HEIC and TIFF.
Crop, resize, rotate and adjust images.
Add markup and export to supported image formats.
steps: Open an image on your Mac.
Make your adjustments and review the pixels.
Export a copy in a format suited to its use.
image-editor.note: Reading and writing support varies by format and macOS codec availability. Some formats can be opened but cannot be saved in their original form.
image-editor.question: Can I resize an image before sharing it?
image-editor.answer: Yes. Resize the image and export a copy. Review the dimensions and choose a format that preserves the transparency or image quality you need.

download.title: Your next office starts here.
download.intro: Choose your platform and check the release status. The source code is available on GitHub.
download.macText: The source targets macOS 14 or later. A public DMG installer has not been released yet.
download.windowsText: Source code for a preliminary Windows version is available on GitHub. An EXE installer has yet to be published.
download.sourceTitle: Build it. Read it. Make it yours.
download.sourceText: Get the MIT-licensed source on GitHub. Building on macOS requires the Xcode Command Line Tools. Local builds use ad-hoc signing unless you configure distribution signing.
download.releaseNote: Download buttons appear when published release files are available. No installer is represented as signed or notarised without release evidence.
download.buildText: Until a signed installer is published, you can build the apps yourself in a few minutes. Run these commands in Terminal.
download.buildStep1: Install Apple's Xcode Command Line Tools.
download.buildStep2: Download the source code from GitHub.
download.buildStep3: Build all six apps, or build one app and copy it to Applications.

about.title: An office with nothing to hide.
about.intro: OFF42 is an independent, open-source family of six native macOS applications. The project brings everyday file work together through a shared interface and common tools.
about.licenseText: Use, study, modify and redistribute the software under the MIT license. The repository includes the license terms and source code.
about.contributeTitle: Better tools are a shared effort.
about.contributeText: Report a reproducible bug, suggest an improvement, help with translations or contribute code through GitHub.
about.honestText: The project is evolving. The repository documents tested builds, limitations and audit coverage. Source availability is separate from packaged, signed and notarised releases.

privacy.title: Keep your work close.
privacy.intro: This website introduces OFF42 and links to the project's source and releases. It does not accept or process your documents.
privacy.siteText: The site has no advertising, analytics scripts or account system. Hosting providers may process request information to deliver and protect the website.
privacy.appText: Core editing in OFF42 runs locally on your Mac. Optional network features, external links and certificate timestamp services involve their respective providers.
privacy.linksText: GitHub and other linked services have their own privacy policies. Your files are not uploaded by visiting this website.
